preamble: Schwa [ə] surfaces as, or historically becomes, the open-mid front vowel [ɛ]. In French the e muet of open syllables alternates with [ɛ] in closed syllables within verb paradigms; in Central Catalan the stressed /ə/ of Eastern Catalan was fronted to /ɛ/; and in Delhi Hindustani /ə/ is realized as [ɛ] around /ɦ/.

examples.note: Schwa of the open syllable alternates with /ɛ/ when the syllable is closed.
Eastern Catalan centralized Proto-Romance stressed /e/ to /ə/; Balearic keeps it and Central Catalan fronted it to /ɛ/.
Conditioned allophone of /ə/ in the sequence /əɦə/; not every speaker has it.

sources: Tranel, B. (1987). The Sounds of French: An Introduction. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511620645
